name: Paternalistic Conservatism
summary: Paternalistic conservatism holds that society is an organic, hierarchical whole in which the privileged owe duties of care to those below, from the feudal idea of noblesse oblige. It uses a benevolent state to keep a safety net, regulate industry and win workers' loyalty, in order to prevent class conflict and revolution, while keeping a market economy, property, monarchy and religion. It is pragmatic and gradualist, rejecting both laissez-faire and socialist planning.
scope: Disraeli's Tory paternalism and Victorian factory reform (Oastler, Sadler, Shaftesbury) and Bismarck's state-led social insurance, with later one-nation and Christian-social heirs. Excludes the free-market right and authoritarian cases such as Chiang's regime. Modern social and foreign-policy issues were mostly not addressed and are low-confidence inferences.

keyFigures.name: Benjamin Disraeli
keyFigures.role: Architect of one-nation Toryism, author of Sybil and Conservative prime minister.

keyFigures.name: Otto von Bismarck
keyFigures.role: Chancellor who built Germany's compulsory social insurance partly to undercut socialism.

keyFigures.name: Anthony Ashley-Cooper, 7th Earl of Shaftesbury
keyFigures.role: Early Tory advocate of Factory Acts and humane treatment of workers.

sources.title: Bismarckian welfare state (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.usedFor: Bismarck's social insurance, its anti-socialist and Christian framing, and employer-administered design

universal-healthcare.rationale: Bismarck's compulsory sickness insurance and the safety-net role the tradition gives the state point to state-guaranteed care, though the model is insurance-based rather than tax-funded.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Paternalists accept wage protection for workers but no source commits them to a substantial rise; adherents split between protecting workers and avoiding disruption of the market.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The tradition keeps a market economy but wants regulation and a safety net, rejecting laissez-faire as the free-market right's critics note; it does not say markets always beat government.

public-ownership.rationale: Sources say it rejects public control of the means of production in favour of a regulated mixed economy, so major-industry nationalisation is not a core demand.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: It supports some redistribution but also defends hierarchy and property, and gives no figure; the elite's duty is framed as care rather than heavy taxation.

unions-good.rationale: Disraeli's government passed trade union laws and the tradition wants workers' loyalty to society, so unions are welcomed as legitimate when they cooperate rather than fight classes.

property-fundamental.rationale: Conservatives defend property as a bulwark of order and the paternalist duty of owners presupposes ownership, though property is conditional on its obligations.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The tradition favours regulation that serves consumers and producers and protects workers, as in the Factory Acts championed by Shaftesbury and Oastler.

cut-welfare.rationale: A social safety net against poverty is the heart of the ideology; Bismarck built social insurance precisely to give workers a stake in the order.

worker-ownership.rationale: It rejects socialist ownership schemes and accepts hierarchy between owners and workers, wanting duty rather than workers' control.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred: paternalists give security and authority weight over individual liberty, which Scruton-style conservatism calls not absolute; the topic was never addressed directly.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from the state's paternal duty to promote the morality and welfare of subjects, which favours restricting harmful substances.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Inferred: paternal moral guardianship favours restrictions, but traditional conservatives also value free speech and the topic is modern; adherents split.

strong-leader.rationale: It favours established institutions and gradual change over a leader bypassing them, though authority is valued; Bismarck's strong-minister model is an exception.

state-harmful.rationale: The state is cast as a benevolent paternal figure that sets goals and maintains a safety net, and Bismarck used it for insurance, so calling it unnecessary or harmful is the opposite stance.

limit-guns.rationale: Never addressed; paternal order favours restriction while rural conservatives resist, so adherents split.

empower-police-military.rationale: Order and strong institutions are central to the Tory case, and Disraeli prized the army and empire; support is moderate not extreme.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the moral-welfare mandate of the paternal state, which treats such trades as harms to be curbed rather than rights.

decide-locally.rationale: Organic conservatism values family and community, but a national welfare state implies central authority; split.

rehabilitation.rationale: Paternal care suggests reform of offenders but conservatives also stress deterrence and order; not clearly addressed.

traditional-family.rationale: Conservatives place faith in family, property and religion as the base of organic society.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred from traditionalist roots in which family and moral custom are preserved; modern paternalists in Britain and elsewhere are divided, so confidence is low.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from the paternal state's duty to promote morality and Christian roots; modern adherents are divided.

more-religion-public.rationale: Religion is treated as a binding force in the tradition, from Stoecker's Protestant workers' party to Coleridge's national church, so a larger public role is welcomed.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Paternal duty to the disadvantaged could support redress, but the strand is class-based and never addressed this; adherents split.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred: traditionalist roots favour inherited roles and distrust constructivist theory.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Disraeli named maintaining the country's institutions as the Tory party's first object, in the Crystal Palace speech.

gradual-change.rationale: Burke's view that a state without means of change lacks means of conservation, and organic development, are core to conservatism and to paternalist reform from above.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Never a defining question for the strand; one-nation unity is inclusive of those inside the nation but adherents divide on numbers.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Inferred from Disraeli's preference for national and imperial institutions over cosmopolitan principles.

free-trade.rationale: Disraeli favoured an imperial tariff, while later paternalists accepted free trade; the strand is divided and pragmatic.

nation-first.rationale: The speech frames the choice as an imperial England against continental cosmopolitan principles, and the national community is the object of paternal duty.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; imperial paternalism supports activism abroad but pragmatism limits it.

open-borders.rationale: Organic national community with obligations among its members is incompatible with open borders; no source supports it.

limit-growth.rationale: Inferred from a pro-business mixed-economy stance that does not question growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Never addressed; state paternalism favours action but conservative caution and cost concerns divide adherents.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Conservatives put prudence and inherited institutions ahead of faith in progress, yet the tradition is not hostile to technology; no stated view.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed; state-led energy security fits, but no source speaks to it.

revolution-justified.rationale: The pragmatic argument is that elite duty prevents revolution; the whole strand aims to forestall it.

experts-over-public.rationale: Paternalists trust a governing class, as Coleridge's clerisy suggests, but democratic Toryism also appeals to the people.

central-planning.rationale: The article states it rejects command or planned economies and public control of means of production.

socialized-markets.rationale: Inferred from rejection of public and collective control of the means of production.

land-value-tax.rationale: Inferred from defence of property and landed interests; never addressed.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred: hereditary property and family continuity are valued, so heavy inheritance taxes are disfavoured.

basic-income.rationale: Paternalist welfare is conditional and structured, as in Bismarck's contribution-based insurance, rather than unconditional cash.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Disraeli backed imperial tariffs while the strand later embraced free trade; adherents split by period.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Japanese LDP paternalism was interventionist but British paternalists were not; split by country.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Property is valued, but the strand does not target concentration versus dispersal.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The tradition keeps a market-based mixed economy and rejects public control of the means of production.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: A regulated market economy with a state role is assumed; free-market monetary radicalism is the opposite pole.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Bismarck's occupational employer organizations that administered accident insurance resemble corporatism, but no general demand for price-setting bodies exists.

one-party-rule.rationale: The strand grows from parliamentary Toryism; only some authoritarian cases such as Chiang's regime blur this, so it is not central.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Disraeli's Tory aim of maintaining the country's institutions includes the Crown, and Bismarck served the Kaiser.

democracy-best.rationale: Tory democracy accepted the vote but the tradition accepts hierarchy and benevolent authority; adherents hold varied views.

direct-votes.rationale: Burke-style conservatism limits participation to the qualified and prefers representative government to plebiscites.

workers-councils.rationale: Political power grounded in workers' own councils overturns the hierarchy in which elites carry duties to those below, so it is rejected.

right-to-secede.rationale: Disraeli feared breakup of the empire and the organic nation is treated as an inseparable whole.

natural-rulers.rationale: Social hierarchy is accepted as natural, with elites carrying duties to those below.

political-violence-never.rationale: Unaddressed; the strand opposes revolution but accepts state force for order.

war-builds-character.rationale: Inferred; the speech favours imperial strength but the strand does not praise war itself.

separate-church-state.rationale: Coleridge's national church and religion as a pillar of order oppose strict separation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Religion is valued as a moral base but legal codes are inherited custom rather than scriptural rule.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The state has a positive duty to maintain order and promote welfare; privatising its core functions contradicts it.

military-superiority.rationale: Disraeli tied the maintenance of a great imperial country to national strength, so keeping superiority over rivals fits the tradition.

ethnic-nation.rationale: One-nation framing unites classes within existing national institutions rather than defining nation by ethnicity.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Class harmony and mutual obligation are the opposite of class conflict.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Hierarchy is accepted as natural; paternalism offers a floor not equality.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Inferred from the centralising, imperial, institution-preserving outlook of Disraeli's Toryism, which gives no special authority to subject peoples.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred from Disraeli's pride in empire and the strand's defence of national institutions.

civilizational-union.rationale: Nation-centred outlook; Disraeli opposed dissolution of imperial unity into other blocs.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Noblesse oblige holds that privilege brings duties to others, so pursuit of self-interest is not praised as a virtue.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Scruton-style conservatism says individual liberty is not absolute, and noblesse oblige centres on duty.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The conservatism covered in the SEP stresses family, property and religion rather than nature's own worth; adherents are split and the topic is rarely addressed.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred from family-centred traditionalism and opposition to coercion.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Coleridge criticised unchecked industrialisation, but the tradition reforms industrial society rather than rejecting it.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Oakeshott prefers stability to improvement and conservatives distrust disruption of institutions.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred from Burke's reliance on inherited wisdom and the paternal state's duty to guard the morality of subjects.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred from preference for judgement of a governing class over rules.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: A modern issue where paternal security concerns pull one way and conservative respect for private life the other, so adherents split.

restore-past-order.rationale: Conservatism values continuity but paternalists reform to adapt; no desire to restore a lost order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The article notes its pragmatism and critics call it non-ideological, though adherents hold paternal principles.

direct-action.rationale: Order and reform from above, not pressure from the street, are the method.

means-match-ends.rationale: No source speaks to this, and paternalists use state authority for benevolent ends without claiming means must mirror them.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Organic civilisation and its institutions are what is to be preserved.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The tradition accepts an industrial market economy and natural social hierarchy, so ending the division of labour is far outside it.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Care for the poor is a floor but distribution mainly by station and market.

production-for-use.rationale: It keeps a market-based mixed economy rather than replacing profit-led production with planned production for need.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The strand rejects socialist analysis; profit is legitimate if owners meet duties.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Working-class rule over former elites reverses the paternal order where a governing class cares for those beneath it.

collective-farming.rationale: Rejection of public control of the means of production and defence of property rules out compulsory collectivised agriculture.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The strand reforms capitalism rather than treating it as doomed, and shares none of the Marxist theory of imperialism.

taxation-theft.rationale: A paternal state funds a social safety net through public revenue, so taxation is legitimate rather than robbery.

harm-principle.rationale: The paternal state promotes the morality and welfare of subjects, not only prevention of harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Organic society puts the community and mutual obligations before individualist rights.

conscription.rationale: Inferred from strong state and military emphasis; modern adherents divide.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Obligations bind members of an organic society; exit is not the check.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is a paternal figure with duties, not a firm with customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Freedom is tied to authority and welfare in this tradition rather than mere non-interference.

media-academia-power.rationale: The sources say nothing on media and universities; adherents differ on whether they now outweigh elected officials.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Class-based paternalism does not rely on racial hierarchy; confidence low as unaddressed.

organic-representation.rationale: Organic society, with representation by station, family and community fits Burke's qualified participation.

total-state.rationale: It accepts a benevolent state but also faith in family, property and religion, not state direction of all life.

national-rebirth.rationale: Paternalists want to reform an existing order gradually and avert unrest, not rebuild the nation through radical rebirth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Disraeli prized maintaining the empire rather than conquering more, and the tradition is not defined by expansion, so adherents split.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Noblesse oblige echoes feudal ideas but modern paternalism works via state institutions.

bound-labor.rationale: Elites owe care, but modern paternalists do not support legal bondage.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Inferred from traditionalist belief in inherited wisdom, not power-based relativism.

universal-morality.rationale: Burke's inherited wisdom is customary, but religious paternalists hold moral truths; split.

single-common-good.rationale: The organic society and elite duty suggest one common good, but it also balances class interests pragmatically.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The sources never address Zionism, and adherents have held varied views, so no position is inferable.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Never addressed in the sources on this strand; adherents have no common position on diaspora citizenship.

revive-national-language.rationale: The tradition values national institutions and culture but takes no documented stand on reviving a lapsed language.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Hierarchy in the workplace is accepted, with duties rather than votes.

school-vouchers.rationale: Inferred: paternal state provides services directly rather than through market choice.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: No stated fiscal rule; Keynesian post-war paternalists accepted deficits, others did not.

economic-freedom.rationale: Disputes the claim that economic liberty alone sustains freedom; state regulation is accepted.

rule-by-example.rationale: Noblesse oblige holds that the privileged lead by responsible example, alongside law.

national-self-determination.rationale: Imperial Toryism valued the empire's unity yet nations' institutions; no clear stand and adherents split.

force-without-un.rationale: An anachronistic question for a 19th-century-rooted tradition, and adherents split between strong national action and legalism.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Burke defended prejudice and custom as latent wisdom and religion as social foundation, against reason as sole guide.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Bismarck's insurance was tied to employment, not citizenship per se; not addressed.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Bismarck's insurance was contribution-based, but modern adherents divide on conditionality.

class-collaboration.rationale: Obligations across classes to avert conflict are explicit in Disraeli's two nations concern.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Disraeli named maintaining the institutions of the country as the Tory party's first object, so sacrificing inherited institutions is rejected.

dominated-front.rationale: Inferred from a Western-oriented, imperial view that sees no reason for a front against leading Western powers.

workers-nation.rationale: Stoecker and Bismarck sought workers' attachment to nation and monarchy.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Traditionalist roots favour inherited roles, but modern paternalists accept equality in public life, so adherents split.

ban-interest.rationale: A market-based mixed economy with ordinary credit is assumed, and nothing in the tradition proposes banning lending at interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The ideology's divisions are class-based with mutual duty across classes; legal racial caste is not part of its documented positions.

state-class-instrument.rationale: It treats the state as a benevolent father to all classes, not an instrument of class domination, which is a Marxist claim.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: No source addresses energy production, and state-minded paternalists and business-minded ones differ.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Organic nation favours shared culture but strand is silent; adherents split.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy of elites to replace a population is not part of this tradition, which defends a governing class's good faith.

proportional-representation.rationale: Inferred from preference for established, stable representative institutions over reform of electoral machinery.

national-mission.rationale: Disraeli's imperial vision was of maintaining empire, not of exporting a political system; adherents split.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Inferred from traditionalist acceptance of hierarchy as natural, which rejects the claim of structural advantage as injustice.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The ideology depends on a governing class that is competent and dutiful, so it rejects the picture of corrupt, out-of-touch elites.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Paternalism stresses care for the weak, and coercive eugenic control over reproduction conflicts with that and with family-centred tradition.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Never addressed; deference to authority and respect for rule of law pull in different directions.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The paternal state sets goals, ensures fair play and keeps a safety net, going well beyond a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not part of its documented class-based paternalism, which concerns duties between classes rather than racial purity.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Hierarchy is accepted as natural, though the Christian roots imply equal worth before God; adherents split on legal equality.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The tradition rejects socialism and exists to forestall it, so a debate about its survival is of no support to it.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Inferred from Disraeli's imperial pride in settler colonies and self-government for them.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Never addressed; tradition respects both unified law and religious custom, so no position can be inferred.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred: religion is valued by the state but compulsion about conversion is not part of its stated programme.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A distinctly Indian religious-nationalist demand with no place in the documented Western paternalist tradition.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Inferred from Coleridge's national church and the role of religion in binding workers to society, which favour religious instruction.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A doctrine specific to Marxist-Leninist states that the tradition does not share.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Authority legitimate when paternal; Burke ties it to tradition; split.

trade-surplus.rationale: Disraeli favoured imperial tariffs yet the strand has no doctrine on trade balances; adherents split.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced removal of minorities is at odds with the aim of binding all classes into one nation.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Conservatives accept state force for order and authority; the absolute prohibition is a libertarian principle.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The strand stresses cooperation among classes and reciprocal duty over struggle between individuals or peoples.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not addressed; order-minded paternalists would accept it but parliamentary Tories value open party competition.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: A republican concept not addressed by the sources; paternal authority fits poorly yet adherents have no stated stance.

separated-powers.rationale: Burke-style conservatism values balanced institutions and checks over unconstrained power.

vanguard-party.rationale: A revolutionary party leading the working class is opposite to the paternal approach that prevents revolution through elite reform.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Disraeli warned that the ruling class must respond to hardship, and the tradition stresses duty to those below.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Wider ownership appeals to Tories but paternal care for tenants pulls the other way; nothing states a position.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The tradition has both backed union legalisation (Disraeli) and order, so adherents split on limits.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Paternalism ascribes poverty to social conditions that elites must remedy, not to numbers of people.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The one-nation concern is class cohesion, and sources give no view on ethnic diversity; adherents split.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Rule by lot ignores qualification and station, which Burke-style conservatism requires of those who govern.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Paternalists value authority and order, but Burke-style constitutionalism distrusts arbitrary power; no source covers emergencies and adherents split.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: A regulated mixed economy permits market intervention, but nothing states support for fixed maximum prices; adherents divide on it.

party-controls-media.rationale: Party control of information belongs to single-party regimes, which the tradition does not endorse.

party-commands-army.rationale: The tradition has the army under the Crown or state, not a ruling party.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Never addressed by the sources; adherents have no common view.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Inferred from accepted hierarchy and the belief that those qualified to govern are not average workers.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Not a documented principle for this tradition, whose pragmatism runs toward flexibility.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Disraeli preferred maintained national and imperial institutions to merging into continental arrangements.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Bismarck's Kaiser commanded the forces while British paternalists accept parliamentary government; split by country.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Coleridge's national church and the hierarchical, organic conception of society favour episcopal order.

clerical-rule.rationale: Religion supports political order in this tradition but statesmen like Disraeli and Bismarck ruled, not clergy.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The nation-first, imperial outlook treats loyalty in war as a duty, never as working for defeat.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The paternal state promotes subjects' morality, yet traditions of free expression divide adherents.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred from Burke's preference for limits on power and established constitutional forms.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall is a plebiscitary check on representatives, which Burke-style conservatism rejects.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Disraeli's vision of an engaged imperial Britain is opposed to withdrawal.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Compelled home ownership has no place in a mixed market economy that retains property relations.

people-in-arms.rationale: Inferred from preference for ordered, professional institutions and hierarchy over arming the citizenry.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Organic traditionalism sometimes praises country life, but the tradition is fundamentally about managing industrial towns.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Bismarck unified Germany, but the strand has no general doctrine on reunification; adherents split.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not addressed by sources; paternal elites are themselves educated, so no common view.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Disraeli's imperial outlook assumed hierarchy among civilizations.

death-penalty.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; order-minded paternalists and Christian humanitarians split.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Moral guardianship suggests caution but modern paternalists accept school education; no stated position.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Inferred: religion valued, yet established-church Toryism has not demanded creationism in schools.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred from the paternal state's duty to promote the morality of subjects, as Beiser's formula has it.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Never addressed; adherents have no common view.

minority-language-support.rationale: Not addressed; national unity pulls one way, paternal care for minorities another.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not addressed; value of religion conflicts with uniform law.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Conservatives treat custom as latent wisdom, against Mill's view that conformity harms development.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Inferred from respect for property and obligations, though paternal duty to the poor might apply abroad.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from an imperial perspective with no push to transform property systems.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Burke-style conservatism opposes rewriting constitutions afresh instead of letting them develop organically.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Chiang's regime is cited as paternal authoritarian, but mainstream adherents do not make this central.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Elite duty is framed within the nation, so no stated view on global aid; adherents split.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Inferred from the national-strength and sovereignty emphasis of Disraeli's Toryism.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Disraeli and Bismarck served hereditary monarchs and the tradition favours inherited heads of state.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Never addressed; adherents split between state oversight and monetary stability.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; split.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The paternal tradition holds that the privileged owe duties to those below, making property a trust rather than an absolute right.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A Marxist dispute not addressed in the tradition.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Never addressed; the state's protective role fits it, while conservative caution about change cuts both ways.

collective-defense.rationale: Inferred from Disraeli's emphasis on imperial unity and national security.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between imperial realism and legality.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Inferred: the tradition values established religion's independence and role in order, rather than curbing it.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Institutions of the country, including the Crown, are meant to stand for national unity above class and faction.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Disraeli feared imperial dissolution, but the strand has no stated doctrine; split.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents split.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Inferred: monarchy is valued as an institution but divine descent is not part of the tradition.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Support for redistribution and a safety net implies progressive rates rather than flat ones.

character-from-environment.rationale: Elite duty to relieve hardship presumes circumstances shape people, though traditionalist views stress inherited nature.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Burke-style constitutionalism opposes a ruler unbound by law.

space-expansion.rationale: Inferred from caution about grand projects and prioritisation of domestic social order.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Burke-influenced conservatism favours balance of orders and institutions of both elite and popular kinds.

leader-cult.rationale: Cult of the leader as embodiment of the nation is alien to institution-based conservatism.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A dispute inside Marxism-Leninism with no bearing on this tradition, which rejects class struggle.

land-redistribution.rationale: Landed property and its duties are defended, so confiscation for redistribution is rejected.

refugee-return.rationale: Never addressed in sources; adherents split.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Inferred from the tradition's focus on existing institutions rather than irredentist claims.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred: religion is valued but legal punishment for leaving it is not part of the tradition.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not part of the documented tradition and at odds with its Western institutional setting.

common-currency.rationale: Never addressed; adherents split between pooling and national monetary control.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The tradition centres on the existing nation and empire, not cross-border unions of kin peoples.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: One-nation framing wants a single national community, not separate self-governing minorities.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no stated position.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Burke and Disraeli stress institutions, moral duty and tradition, against economic determinism.

ban-cartels.rationale: Support for regulation serving consumers and producers could imply anti-cartel rules, but nothing states it.

no-bailouts.rationale: Never addressed; paternal state protectiveness conflicts with market discipline, so adherents split.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Inferred from Burke's wish to temper majority will with tradition and established institutions.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from traditionalist acceptance of natural hierarchy, which does not require mandated parity.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Disraeli favoured an imperial tariff, but a closed bloc shut off from outside trade goes beyond the tradition.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Support for regulation protecting workers suggests it, but modern trade deals were never addressed.

moral-incentives.rationale: Duty is emphasised but wages and material incentives remain in the market economy; adherents split.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The tradition aims at preventing revolution through reform from above.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Social hierarchy is accepted as natural and noblesse oblige derives from feudal privilege.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Preserving national institutions and traditions favours teaching history centred on the nation.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred from Disraeli's imperial paternalism toward colonies and the paternal state's own logic.

patriotic-education.rationale: Maintaining national institutions as the Tory first object implies schools teaching loyalty.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not addressed; the class-based strand has no established view.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred: the tradition keeps the existing market economy and banking system.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Disraeli's pragmatic argument is that reform answers hardship and preserves the order against revolutionary collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Disraeli made maintaining the empire a Tory object, so cultivating influence in former imperial regions fits.

delink-world-market.rationale: A market-based mixed economy is assumed; withdrawing from rich-country economic ties finds no place in it.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist claim about exploitation that the tradition does not share.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Regulation serving consumers and producers and a paternal view of fair play oppose unrestricted refusal of service.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Inferred from Burke's preference for evolving custom and parliamentary institutions over written constitutional limits.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Noblesse oblige is the defining principle of the tradition, and Disraeli warned that a ruling class that ignores hardship invites revolution.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Disraeli's imperial outlook and preference for established arrangements.

elective-rulers.rationale: Paternalistic conservatives defend the Crown and hierarchy; inferred from Disraeli's constitutional-monarchy outlook.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred from the hierarchical Burkean tradition that values collective order over individual vetoes.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from the conservative constitutionalism of Burke and Disraeli, which allows resistance to unlawful rule.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Disraeli worked within a parliamentary system balanced by Crown and Lords; inferred, with the monarchy kept as symbol.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Victorian reformers such as Shaftesbury supported animal protection; not a core paternalist theme.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred from the traditional acceptance of animal use with limits on cruelty.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Duty of the governing class to take part in public life is central to the Tory paternalist idea; inferred.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the hierarchical conservative view that culture upholds social ties rather than domination.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Marxist-Gramscian claim foreign to paternalist conservatism; inferred.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred from Disraeli's imperial outlook; dependency theory is an anachronism for this strand.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from the national-community emphasis of Disraeli's Toryism, which put 'the nation' above class.

party-own-road.rationale: Not applicable to paternalist conservatism; adherents would have no stake.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Paternalists favour state guidance and welfare over self-reliance, so the rule is inferred as disagreed.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Bismarckian and Disraelian statecraft was realist, not irredentist; inferred.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the support for existing social hierarchy and the national community.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anachronistic for this strand; adherents would not take a position.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred from the conservative condemnation of both left and right extremes; an anachronism for this strand.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from British abolition and mainstream historical accounts.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from the conservative value of continuity and heritage.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Burkean conservatism, which this strand draws on, holds that institutions grow from a people's history and cannot simply be transplanted.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Bismarck's Prussia was an exception but paternalists generally hold with civilian government; inferred.

paid-care-work.rationale: Paternalists support welfare for families but did not address domestic labour; adherents' view is inferred as split.

filial-duty.rationale: Organic-society conservatism stresses reciprocal duties across generations and the family as a social bond; inferred from that, as filial duty is not a stated plank.

office-by-exam.rationale: Adherents split between the traditional view that office suits the gentry and the Victorian reform of merit-based civil service; the doctrine does not settle it.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Disraeli's emphasis on national institutions and a regulating state suggests support for protecting strategic industries; inferred, not stated.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Paternalist conservatism upholds religion and the family as stabilising institutions, so adherents would likely resist easy divorce; inferred.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Burkean tradition holds that representatives exercise independent judgment rather than act as instructed delegates, and it favours hierarchy and gradual change.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Bismarck's pay-as-you-go-style state social insurance and the tradition's rejection of laissez-faire favour collective state provision over private individual accounts.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The tradition keeps private property and inherited landed hierarchy while rejecting socialist planning, so it opposes use-based communal tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Disraeli's Tory tradition worked within parliamentary monarchy and constitutional institutions; supply control by Parliament is inferred as accepted.

single-official-language.rationale: Its stress on national institutions and cohesion suggests support for a common national language; inferred, as the doctrine is mostly silent.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The doctrine does not address the issue and adherents are split between national-property instincts and respect for property rights.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Gradualist, pragmatic conservatism distrusts outcome-based legal doctrines; inferred from its stress on intent, hierarchy and tradition.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The tradition's stress on duty, religion and organic community over acquisitiveness suggests sympathy with the critique; inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Pragmatic, order-focused conservatism favours stable authority and avoids revolutionary methods; Disraeli's focus was on empire and institutions. Inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Not addressed; imperial-minded Tories valued maintaining spheres of influence, but the tradition also stresses prudence and national interest, so adherents are split.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred from its duty of the privileged to those below and regulation of industry, which implies wariness of business power over government.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Not addressed by the tradition and nothing in its principles settles it.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred from its concern with family, social cohesion and state support for welfare; population policy was not a theme.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not addressed; an organic, local society favours it but the tradition kept property rights intact.

job-guarantee.rationale: It built a safety net and factory regulation but kept the market economy, and never promised work to all.

democratic-peace.rationale: Inferred from its scepticism of democracy and its imperial, statecraft focus.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: It treats society as an organic hierarchy that wins loyalty through duties of care, so obedience to the established order is expected.

non-intervention.rationale: Disraeli-style imperial statecraft implies states act in their own interest; inferred, not stated.

industrial-unions.rationale: Inferred from its aim to win workers' loyalty by reform and class harmony; union structure was not a theme.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Inferred from its aim of class harmony and organic unity, which leaves no place for minority conspiracy theories.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: It keeps the church, monarchy and family as institutions of the organic society.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from the Victorian and Bismarckian view that governing is for trained elites; no open-records principle existed.

informal-organisation.rationale: It rests on hierarchy, established institutions and duties of care from the top down, not on informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred from its nationalist and imperial outlook, which sets national interest first.

religious-nation.rationale: Disraeli backed the established church yet accepted Jews and others in the nation; adherents split.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Disraeli backed empire and imperial primacy, but the doctrine says nothing of tribute or ritual submission by other states. Inferred.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The tradition stresses duty of the better off to those below within one nation, which implies sharing between regions rather than retention. Inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Paternalists kept property and a market economy but rejected socialist planning and common ownership of production, so they would not endorse the formula as stated. Inferred.

defeat-communism.rationale: The welfare policy of Bismarck and Disraeli was framed to head off socialism and revolution, and the tradition opposes socialist planning, so defeating rather than coexisting fits.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The tradition keeps a market economy and a safety net and Bismarck's insurance was employer- and worker-administered rather than run directly by the state, which fits a mixed provider system.

religion-illusion.rationale: Paternalists defend religion and the church as pillars of an organic, hierarchical society, so they would reject the view of religion as an illusion that fades.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The tradition keeps a market economy and property and values the wealth industry creates, while opposing socialist planning, so it can credit capitalism as a foundation. Inferred from its acceptance of markets.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The tradition defends the family and keeps the existing order; it seeks reform of conditions through paternal duty, not transformation of the economic system.

socialized-care.rationale: Organic-society conservatism treats the family as a core institution, so public replacement of household work is unlikely, though state support for families fits. Inferred.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not a doctrinal issue; pragmatic, gradualist conservatives view language as an inherited institution to be conserved rather than purged by policy. Inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: The tradition values inherited duties and settled obligations, so lasting treaties fit, though it did not address the question directly. Inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The tradition is hierarchical and monarchist and keeps property and the state, so communities holding property in common contradict it.

majority-settlement.rationale: Disraeli's one-nation idea stresses unity but there is no doctrine on steering settlement into minority regions; adherents split.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Paternalists reject both laissez-faire and socialist planning, taking a middle course that preserves property and class duty, which fits a third way.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The tradition's concern is class duty, not land claims; adherents are split and the sources are silent.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Inferred: nothing in the tradition supports denial and its modern heirs reject it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Victorian adherents accepted such laws, while modern one-nation heirs mostly do not; the doctrine is silent so it is a split.

suppress-opposition.rationale: It aims to head off revolution through reform rather than repression, though Bismarck paired welfare with anti-socialist laws; inferred.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: It keeps religion and the established church but is pragmatic and gradualist, so punishing false religion is unlikely; inferred.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Disraeli championed the empire as a national good, but the statement's economic-benefit focus is inferred rather than stated.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: An Islamic religious-law question the tradition never addressed.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The tradition values gradual change, monarchy and order, so forcible removal of rulers is rejected; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: It holds that society is a hierarchy in which the privileged care for those below, rather than one governed by direct popular decision-making; inferred.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Inferred: it treats class as bridged by duty and loyalty, not as a system of overlapping oppressions.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The tradition predates the issue; inferred from its traditional social outlook.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred from its religious and traditional moral outlook.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: One-nation conservatives see themselves on the right yet reject both laissez-faire and socialism, but the claim that left and right are obsolete is not theirs; inferred.

alienated-labor.rationale: Factory reformers such as Oastler and Shaftesbury attacked harsh conditions, but they did not use the Marxist concept; split.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The tradition did not address it and modern heirs are split.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: It keeps monarchy and religion as parts of the organic order, but no source says authority is from God; inferred.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: It upholds religion in public life, so barring religious dress is unlikely; inferred.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred from its use of the state to protect weaker parties against employers.

social-market-economy.rationale: It keeps a market economy with a safety net and industrial regulation, rejecting both laissez-faire and state planning, which is this statement.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Defence of the realm and crown is part of its order; inferred.

rich-first.rationale: Noblesse oblige holds that the privileged owe duties to those below, so letting some grow rich first is uneasy; inferred.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The tradition did not address it and heirs are split between alliances and independence.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inferred: the tradition keeps monarchy and hereditary institutions as part of an organic social order (Disraeli's defence of crown and aristocracy).

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred: it prefers state social insurance and paternal oversight to user-owned banking; no source discusses this.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred: it prizes national self-sufficiency and imperial pride but accepted financial orthodoxy; no source discusses lenders.

property-franchise.rationale: Inferred: Disraeli's 1867 reform enlarged the franchise to working men to win their loyalty, so adherents do not seek wealth bars.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Inferred: the tradition upholds hierarchy and duty within a settled order and has no ecological-feminist strand.

reification.rationale: Inferred: it holds that capitalism needs paternal regulation, but it does not use the Marxist concept of reification.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred: it defends private property and existing institutions and answers inequality through duty and welfare, not by questioning press freedom.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred: it defends established law and gradual reform through legitimate institutions, though paternal discretion is also valued.

racial-franchise.rationale: Inferred: it appeals to a shared nation across classes, though imperial paternalism was often racially hierarchical; no source supports an ethnic franchise.

online-participation.rationale: Inferred: not addressed by this 19th-century tradition and adherents' views are split.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred: not addressed; the tradition values accountable institutions but also elite discretion.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inferred: the tradition values religion's social role but prefers inclusive national unity to legal bars on marriage.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred: it seeks class harmony and duty toward all below, which conflicts with shunning a minority's businesses.

citizens-assembly.rationale: The tradition trusts a hierarchical society led by a dutiful elite and an organised state, not rule by ordinary citizens chosen by lot; inferred from its organic, elite-stewardship view.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Paternalists treat established religion and tradition as a social bond to be preserved, with gradual change only; inferred from that conservative stance, as the sources do not address doctrinal reform.

missingStatements.text: The wealthy and privileged have a duty to look after those less fortunate than themselves.
missingStatements.rationale: Noblesse oblige is the defining principle of the tradition, and Disraeli warned that a ruling class that ignores hardship invites revolution.

notes: Strongly contested between Tory and German strands and with free-market critics who call it right-wing socialism. Sources s3 and s4 were read in part only. Disraeli favoured imperial tariffs while later paternalists accepted free trade.
